info.title: AI Research Assistant
info.description: Backend API for the AI Research Assistant platform.

post.description:
Authenticate a user and return
access and refresh tokens.

Exchange a valid refresh token for
a new access and refresh token pair.

This endpoint intentionally does NOT use
CurrentUserId because the access token may
already be expired.

get.description:
Return the currently authenticated user.

Requires:

    Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

post.description:
Create a document record from an uploaded file.

Current responsibility:
    - Validate the uploaded file.
    - Create the document metadata record.

Actual document downloading, extraction, parsing, storage,
chunking, embedding, and indexing belong to the Phase 2
document ingestion pipeline.

get.description:
Return documents.

If `paper_id` is supplied, only documents belonging to that
paper are returned.

Examples:
    GET /api/v1/documents
    GET /api/v1/documents?paper_id=7
Return a single document by ID.

post.description: Execute the research retrieval pipeline over the available knowledge base.
Execute a research exploration query through direct retrieval or the Adaptive RAG pipeline.

get.description:
Return the research graph.

This endpoint currently provides the graph API contract expected
by the frontend. Database-backed graph construction can be added
as the graph domain/service layer is implemented.

schema.title: Response Get Graph Api V1 Graph Get

post.description:
Execute the complete research workflow and persist the execution.

Flow with collection_id:

    ResearchQuery
         |
         v
    Validate user
         |
         v
    Extract research question
         |
         v
    Validate collection ownership
         |
         v
    Collection -> Papers -> Documents
         |
         v
    allowed_document_ids
         |
         v
    ResearchPipeline
         |
         +-------------------------+
         |                         |
         v                         v
    Shared Retrieval           LLM Pipeline
    IndexRegistry              OpenRouter
         |                         |
         +------------+------------+
                      |
                      v
                ResearchReport
                      |
                      v
                ResearchResult

Without collection_id, the existing global research behavior is retained.

ExploreRequest.title: ExploreRequest
ExploreRequest.description:
Public API request for the Explore endpoint.

Explore is the application-level entry point. It can either execute
retrieval directly or route the query through Adaptive RAG.

ExploreResponse.title: ExploreResponse
ExploreResponse.description: Public API response returned by the Explore endpoint.

PaperSearchResult.title: PaperSearchResult
PaperSearchResult.description:
Lightweight paper representation returned by search.

`id` may represent:
    - canonical database ID for locally stored papers
    - provider-specific identifier for external results

The service is responsible for deciding which identifier to expose.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description:
Source information for a retrieved chunk.

Important ID conventions:

- papers.id -> INTEGER
- document_chunks.id -> UUID
- document_chunks.document_id -> UUID

QueryAnalysis.title: QueryAnalysis
QueryAnalysis.description: Structured analysis of the user's retrieval query.

RefreshTokenRequest.title: RefreshTokenRequest
RefreshTokenRequest.description:
Request body used to exchange a refresh token
for a new access/refresh token pair.

ReportContent.title: ReportContent
ReportContent.description:
Structured body of a generated research report.

All fields are JSON serializable so the object can be stored
directly in PostgreSQL JSON/JSONB.

ReportCreate.title: ReportCreate
ReportCreate.description: Request used for creating or generating a research report.

ReportEvidence.title: ReportEvidence
ReportEvidence.description:
Traceable evidence used by a research report.

`chunk_id` is intentionally a string because document chunks
in the research system may use UUID identifiers.

ReportListItem.title: ReportListItem
ReportListItem.description: Lightweight report representation for report history.

ReportResponse.title: ReportResponse
ReportResponse.description:
API representation of a research report.

The database model uses `report_metadata`, while the public
API exposes that field as `metadata`.

ReportStatus.title: ReportStatus
ReportStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a research report.

collection_id.title: Collection Id
collection_id.description: Knowledge-base collection to restrict research retrieval to

ResearchQuery.title: ResearchQuery
ResearchQuery.description:
User research request.

Examples:
    "Compare LoRA and QLoRA fine tuning methods"
    "What are the latest approaches to RAG evaluation?"
    "Explain transformer architecture and its limitations"

Canonical request field:
    question

IMPORTANT:
    `question` is the public API field sent by the frontend.

    Internal research pipeline objects may continue to use `query`
    where appropriate. The API request itself must use `question`.

ResearchReport.title: ResearchReport
ResearchReport.description:
Final generated research output.

Returned directly by:

    POST /api/v1/research

ResearchSource.title: ResearchSource
ResearchSource.description:
Represents any information source.

Examples:
    - arXiv paper
    - GitHub repository
    - Documentation page
    - Web page

paper_id.title: Paper Id
paper_id.description: Restrict retrieval to a specific paper ID.

document_id.title: Document Id
document_id.description: Restrict retrieval to a specific document.

RetrievalRequest.title: RetrievalRequest
RetrievalRequest.description:
Request payload for knowledge retrieval.

ID conventions:

- paper_id -> papers.id -> INTEGER
- document_id -> UUID

RetrievalResult.title: RetrievalResult
RetrievalResult.description:
Canonical representation of one retrieved knowledge chunk.

This is the primary backend/frontend retrieval contract.

ID conventions:

- chunk_id -> UUID
- document_id -> UUID
- paper_id -> INTEGER
- section_id -> UUID

app__research__models__Evidence.title: Evidence
app__research__models__Evidence.description: A piece of supporting research evidence.

app__schemas__retrieval__Evidence.title: Evidence
app__schemas__retrieval__Evidence.description:
Evidence associated with a retrieved result.

This provides the retrieval layer with a stable structure that can
later be consumed by citation, reasoning, and report-generation layers.
